title: Control Logic Synthesis: Drawing the Rest of the OWL
problem: SoC design requires complex coordination between architectural specifications, microarchitectural datapaths with functional units, and control logic that orchestrates them. Hardware designers lack automated tools that can synthesize correct control logic with both agility and correctness guarantees.
motivation: Hardware specialization is now ubiquitous rather than exceptional, requiring new automated design tools to implement specialized architectures rapidly and correctly.
method: The approach automatically generates control logic by analyzing three interconnected design layers: architectural specifications (the high-level blueprint), microarchitectural datapath components (the actual hardware devices like functional units), and the control signals needed to coordinate them. Instead of designers hand-writing this coordination logic, an automated process reasons about the dependencies between these layers and automatically generates control logic that orchestrates them correctly. By treating specifications, hardware, and control signals as one unified design problem rather than separate design stages, the tool produces control logic that integrates properly with the hardware.
key_novelty: It automatically generates control logic by treating architecture specifications, hardware components, and control signals as one unified design problem.
contributions: Automated control logic synthesis framework for SoC design
Integration of architectural specification, datapath, and control logic reasoning
Design methodology enabling rapid hardware specialization with correctness
limitations: Specific evaluation results, performance baselines, and practical limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: automated control logic synthesis for hardware design
